canonical_statement: Scriptural texts function primarily as vehicles for spiritual consciousness rather than as objects of historical or intellectual inquiry.

attributions.surface_quote: Its appeal must be primarily to the spiritual consciousness.

canonical_statement: Spiritual wisdom is categorized into ritualistic action for preparation and philosophical discrimination for ultimate vision.

attributions.surface_quote: Karma-Kanda deals with rituals... Upanishad deals wholly with the essentials of philosophic discrimination.

canonical_statement: The Upanishads constitute the final goal or culmination of all wisdom.

attributions.surface_quote: Upanishads are known as the Vedanta, that is, the end or final goal of wisdom.

canonical_statement: The Upanishads are direct revelations of divine origin rather than human compositions.

attributions.surface_quote: Upanishads being regarded as direct revelations of God; while the Smritis... were traditional works of purely human origin.

canonical_statement: Truth exists independently of its written record or historical origin.

attributions.surface_quote: No date for the origin of the Upanishads can be fixed, because the written text does not limit their antiquity.

canonical_statement: The individual soul (Atman) and the ultimate reality (Brahman) are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: Tat tvam asi (That thou art) and Aham Brahmasmi (I am Brahman).

canonical_statement: The fundamental truth of existence is the unity of all life.

attributions.surface_quote: This dominant ideal of the unity of all life and the oneness of Truth.

canonical_statement: The ultimate secret of nature and reality is accessible only through internal introspection.

attributions.surface_quote: The key can only be found where alone the secret of nature lies open to us from within.

canonical_statement: The Upanishads function as pedagogical instruments for the attainment of divine and self-referential knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: They grew up essentially as text books of God-knowledge and Self-knowledge.

canonical_statement: Cognitive tranquility and the withdrawal of sensory energy are necessary preconditions for understanding metaphysical truths.

attributions.surface_quote: It is not possible to comprehend the subtle problems of life unless the thought is tranquil.

canonical_statement: Ancient metaphysical concepts possess a structural incompatibility with modern linguistic frameworks.

attributions.surface_quote: Modern words are round, ancient words are square.

canonical_statement: Spiritual realization requires an internal state of harmony and non-attachment to worldly distractions.

attributions.surface_quote: No study is of avail so long as our inner being is not attuned.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and the Supreme Being are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: Oneness of the Soul and God... are the leading themes.

canonical_statement: Action performed without self-knowledge binds the individual to temporary states rather than liberation.

attributions.surface_quote: Works alone... must inevitably bind a man, unless through them he gains knowledge.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is an infinite totality from which the phenomenal world emerges without diminishing the source.

attributions.surface_quote: From the Invisible Whole comes forth the visible whole... the Whole remains unaltered.

canonical_statement: The Absolute transcends linguistic definition due to its infinite nature.

attributions.surface_quote: God, who is infinite and unbounded, cannot be expressed by finite language.

canonical_statement: The phenomenal world and the Absolute are fundamentally inseparable.

attributions.surface_quote: In the light of true wisdom the phenomenal and the Absolute are inseparable.

canonical_statement: All manifestation is a modification of a singular, unchanging totality.

attributions.surface_quote: all manifestation is merely a modification of the One Supreme Whole

canonical_statement: Perceiving the Divine in all things dissolves the illusion of diversity.

attributions.surface_quote: conception of diversity naturally drops away; because the One Cosmic Existence shines through all things

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the true Self acts as the ultimate sustainer and protector of the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: knowledge of our true Self is the greatest protector and sustainer

canonical_statement: Actions performed with selfish desire bind the soul to the cycle of birth and death.

attributions.surface_quote: actions performed clinging blindly to his lower desires, then his actions bind him

canonical_statement: Actions performed as a surrender to the Divine purify and liberate the soul.

attributions.surface_quote: when the same actions are performed with surrender to God, they purify and liberate him

attributions.surface_quote: condition of heaven and hell is only temporary; because our actions, being finite

canonical_statement: The immortal Soul is fundamentally indestructible.

attributions.surface_quote: How can the immortal Soul ever be destroyed? It cannot be destroyed

canonical_statement: Ignorance of the true Self constitutes the only form of existential suffering or hell.

attributions.surface_quote: the only hell is absence of knowledge

attributions.surface_quote: he who clings to the perishable body... must experience death many times

attributions.surface_quote: The Atman, however, is present everywhere

attributions.surface_quote: all living things must draw their life from the Cosmic Self

attributions.surface_quote: the Self... the true basis of our existence.

attributions.surface_quote: he who knows at the same time both Vidya and Avidya, crosses over death

canonical_statement: The individual Soul and the Supreme Being are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul and God are one and inseparable

attributions.surface_quote: he who knows at the same time both the Unmanifested and the manifested

attributions.surface_quote: no perfect knowledge is possible without simultaneous comprehension of both.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and the Supreme Being are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: The Purusha who dwells within Thee, I am He.

attributions.surface_quote: distinction between the mortal body and the immortal

attributions.surface_quote: face of Truth is hidden by a golden disk.

attributions.surface_quote: my delusion is destroyed... I am one with the Supreme

attributions.surface_quote: death is nothing more than the casting-off of a worn-out garment.

attributions.surface_quote: A guest is the representative of God.

attributions.surface_quote: There is one part of us which must die; there is another part which never dies.

attributions.surface_quote: It is subtler than the subtle and beyond argument.

attributions.surface_quote: no amount of observance of rituals and ceremonies can earn the imperishable.

attributions.surface_quote: seated in the innermost recess, hidden in the cave of the heart.

attributions.surface_quote: is liberated from the fetters of joy and sorrow.

attributions.surface_quote: Self is never born, nor does It die. It did not spring from anything.

attributions.surface_quote: It is both stationary and moving, and It is the basis of all forms.

attributions.surface_quote: It cannot be perceived by the senses; a finer spiritual sight is required.

attributions.surface_quote: Whatever exists in the universe... must spring from It.

attributions.surface_quote: Direct perception of God is possible for those alone who are pure in heart.

attributions.surface_quote: Life and death alike are food for Him.

attributions.surface_quote: The two signify the Higher Self and the lower self, dwelling in the heart.

attributions.surface_quote: Higher Self is like a light and the lower self like a shadow.

attributions.surface_quote: knowledge of Brahman, the Supreme, in both manifested and unmanifested form.

attributions.surface_quote: above this is the Purusha or Supreme Self. Than this there is nothing higher.

attributions.surface_quote: only those who have direct vision of Truth are capable of teaching It.

attributions.surface_quote: That which is soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying; also tasteless, odorless, and eternal.

attributions.surface_quote: When He shines, everything shines after Him; by His light all is lighted.

attributions.surface_quote: Commanded by whom does the life-force move? What power directs the eye and the ear?

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is the transcendent substrate that enables the operation of all sensory and cognitive faculties.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the eye of the eye.

canonical_statement: Human mortality is a consequence of identifying exclusively with the physical body and sensory phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: One who clings to the senses and to things that are ephemeral, must die many deaths.

canonical_statement: Immortality is achieved by transcending the physical nature and realizing the eternal essence within.

attributions.surface_quote: Immortality is attained when man transcends his apparent nature and finds that subtle, eternal essence.

canonical_statement: The ultimate essence is beyond the reach of finite sensory perception, language, and intellectual comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: It is distinct from the known and also It is beyond the unknown.

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Brahman) is beyond the reach of finite sensory perception and intellectual comprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: He is unknowable to man's finite nature.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is the underlying substrate that enables all sensory and cognitive functions.

attributions.surface_quote: THAT which cannot be thought by mind, but by which mind is able to think.

canonical_statement: Beyond the three ordinary states of consciousness (waking, dreaming, sleeping) exists a fourth, superconscious state.

attributions.surface_quote: There is, however, a fourth state, the superconscious, which transcends these.

canonical_statement: The Absolute can only be apprehended when the mind is purified and illuminated by Cosmic Intelligence.

attributions.surface_quote: He can be known, however, by the purified mind only.

canonical_statement: Intellectual certainty regarding the nature of the Absolute is an indicator of ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: If thou thinkest 'I know It well,' then it is certain that thou knowest but little.

canonical_statement: True knowledge of the ultimate reality is achieved only through direct experiential union, not intellectual apprehension.

attributions.surface_quote: Mere intellectual recognition will not give you true knowledge of It.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, exists beyond the reach of sensory perception, speech, and the conceptual mind.

attributions.surface_quote: There the eye does not go, nor speech, nor mind.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is simultaneously beyond the known and the unknown, transcending binary categorization.

attributions.surface_quote: That is distinct from known and also It is beyond the unknown.

canonical_statement: Individual existence is derived from the ultimate reality, making the act of seeking a form of inherent, non-conceptual knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: The very fact that I exist... shows that I know; for It is the source of my being.

canonical_statement: Attaining soul-consciousness requires transcending the relative knowledge of material phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: One who wishes to attain Soul-consciousness must rise above matter.

canonical_statement: Empirical science is limited because it relies on sense perception and excludes the infinite.

attributions.surface_quote: Material science being confined to the sense plane, it ignores what is beyond.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, is beyond the reach of mind, speech, and sense perception.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is unthinkable, because unconditioned.

canonical_statement: True knowledge of the infinite is characterized by the recognition of its unknowability.

attributions.surface_quote: He who thinks he knows It not, knows It.

canonical_statement: The true self is the underlying subject that enables perception, rather than the object of perception.

attributions.surface_quote: The real Self is that within by which he hears and speaks and sees.

canonical_statement: Immortality is attained by realizing the self as the unchanging essence underlying all states of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is known, when It is known in every state of consciousness.

canonical_statement: The individual essence remains untouched by the decay and death of the physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: Although his body may decay and die, the subtle essence of his being remains untouched.

canonical_statement: Individual power derived from physical or mental effort is finite and cannot overcome death.

attributions.surface_quote: strength from muscle and brain is limited and cannot lift one beyond death

canonical_statement: Immortality is achieved exclusively through the direct realization of the Self (Atma-jnana).

attributions.surface_quote: through Self-knowledge immortality is reached

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Brahman) is the singular, non-dual source of all manifested existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is the Absolute, the One without a second, the essence of all

canonical_statement: All individual entities are dependent manifestations of the Absolute, lacking independent existence.

attributions.surface_quote: No manifested form of life can be independent of its source

canonical_statement: The Absolute is the sole agent of all action in the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: He is the only Doer. Nothing moves without that Power.

canonical_statement: Personal deities are limited aspects of the Absolute and cannot represent the totality of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: no one of these can fully represent the Whole

canonical_statement: The Absolute is inherently unknowable and unthinkable in its pure state.

attributions.surface_quote: The Absolute is declared to be unknowable and unthinkable.

canonical_statement: The Absolute manifests in personal, deified forms to facilitate comprehension by seekers.

attributions.surface_quote: He assumes deified personal aspects to make Himself known to His devotees.

canonical_statement: Individual agency is an illusion; all action is derived from the power of the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: It is through His power that you live and act.

canonical_statement: The belief in independent individual achievement is a product of ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: Your idea that 'This victory is ours' is based on ignorance.

canonical_statement: Proximity to the Absolute is determined by the degree of cognitive realization of the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: Indra excels other Devas, because he came nearest to Brahman.

canonical_statement: Proximity to the Supreme Reality is determined by the degree of purity of the consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: they were able to do this because they were purer

canonical_statement: Direct realization of the Supreme Reality constitutes the highest state of being.

attributions.surface_quote: Indra stands as the head of the Devas, because he realized the Truth directly

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality is the sole agent of all action.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is the only Doer.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality transcends all definite forms and is essentially unfathomable.

attributions.surface_quote: the whole of the unfathomable Brahman could not be seen in any definite form

canonical_statement: The human mind serves as the primary instrument for conceptualizing and approaching the Supreme Reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Only by the mind can the seeker after knowledge approach Brahman

canonical_statement: A purified mind functions as a reflective medium for the manifestation of Divine Glory.

attributions.surface_quote: when by constant thought of Him the mind becomes purified, then like a polished mirror it can reflect His Divine Glory.

canonical_statement: The individual who realizes their identity with the Divine becomes a conduit for universal grace.

attributions.surface_quote: Whoever knows Him... serves as a clear channel through which the blessings of Brahman flow.

canonical_statement: All phenomenal existence originates from and eventually returns to a single, unified source.

attributions.surface_quote: One tremendous Whole becoming the world, and again the world merging in that Whole.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is the non-perceivable substrate that enables all sensory and cognitive functions.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the eye of the eye, the ear of the ear... which enables sense-faculties.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality transcends both the known and the unknown, rendering it inaccessible to intellect or sensory perception.

attributions.surface_quote: It is distinct from the known and also It is beyond the unknown.

canonical_statement: True knowledge of the ultimate reality is achieved only by recognizing it as the foundation of all consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: It can be known by him who knows It as the basis of all consciousness.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is infinite and transcends the capacity of conceptual knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: The knower of Truth says, 'I know It not,' because he realizes the unbounded nature.

canonical_statement: The divine essence permeates both the manifest and unmanifest dimensions of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou art this, Thou art That, and Thou art all that is beyond.

canonical_statement: True knowledge encompasses both sensory experience and spiritual intuition.

attributions.surface_quote: He has all the knowledge that comes from the senses and all that comes from Spirit.

canonical_statement: Human mortality is a consequence of identifying the self with the ego, body, and mind.

attributions.surface_quote: Mortals become mortals because they fall under the sway of ego.

canonical_statement: All agency and power originate solely from the divine, rendering individual autonomy an illusion.

attributions.surface_quote: There is no real power, no real doer except God.

canonical_statement: Realizing the divine as the substrate of the self leads to the transcendence of death.

attributions.surface_quote: When we realize Him as the underlying Reality, we transcend death and become immortal.

canonical_statement: Spiritual knowledge is transmitted directly from the consciousness of an illumined teacher to the disciple.

attributions.surface_quote: partaking of the light that streams from the mind of the master to the disciple

canonical_statement: True wisdom is an inner realization that transcends the literal text of scriptures.

attributions.surface_quote: learning was only a cloak for his inner realization

canonical_statement: The Absolute can be known through a singular gnosis that encompasses all other knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: What is that, by knowing which everything else becomes known?

canonical_statement: Supreme wisdom is inaccessible through ritual, scripture, or moral action alone.

attributions.surface_quote: Supreme Wisdom cannot be attained by superficial study, religious rites, or good works.

canonical_statement: The realization of the Absolute requires the purification of the self through renunciation and meditation.

attributions.surface_quote: It can only be realized by the man of meditation, one who has been purified.

canonical_statement: The attainment of ultimate truth necessitates the stripping away of all non-essential mental constructs.

attributions.surface_quote: The Upanishad itself is shorn of all non-essentials.

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Brahman) is the foundational reality from which all other knowledge is derived.

attributions.surface_quote: knowledge of Brahman which is the foundation of all knowledge.

canonical_statement: The personal aspect of Deity (Brahma) acts as the creative power of the universe, distinct from the Absolute (Brahman).

attributions.surface_quote: Brahma is the personal aspect of Deity as distinguished from Brahman, the Absolute.

canonical_statement: Divine beings (Devas) are manifestations of specific qualities of the Divine, functioning as administrators of creation.

attributions.surface_quote: Devas are Bright Beings, each manifesting some special Divine quality and holding some office.

canonical_statement: There exists a fundamental distinction between lower, intellectual knowledge and higher, direct knowledge of the Imperishable.

attributions.surface_quote: There are two kinds of knowledge to be known... higher knowledge and lower knowledge.

canonical_statement: Direct experiential realization of ultimate truth is superior to theoretical or intellectual knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: theoretical knowledge must always be inferior to knowledge based on direct experience.

canonical_statement: The ultimate source of reality is unconditioned, attribute-less, and imperceptible to sensory or intellectual faculties.

attributions.surface_quote: That which cannot be seen... has no origin and no attributes

canonical_statement: Ultimate realization requires the cessation of sensory and intellectual turbulence through meditative serenity.

attributions.surface_quote: It dawns in the soul only when senses, mind and intellect have become pacified.

canonical_statement: The universe manifests as an expansion or emanation from the Imperishable Source.

attributions.surface_quote: does the universe come forth from the Imperishable.

canonical_statement: The creative process of the universe originates from the wisdom and internal energy of the Supreme.

attributions.surface_quote: Out of this fire of wisdom... come forth, first the creative power, and thence all forms.

canonical_statement: Knowledge is categorized into lower knowledge, pertaining to intellectual and ritualistic pursuits, and higher knowledge, pertaining to ultimate truth.

attributions.surface_quote: The Vedic teaching is divided into two distinct parts: Karma-Kanda and Jnana-Kanda.

canonical_statement: Ritual sacrifice serves as a mechanism to test the practitioner's detachment from worldly desires.

attributions.surface_quote: To test whether his mind is wholly free from desire for earthly rewards.

canonical_statement: The universe is structured into seven hierarchical planes or worlds corresponding to grades of experience.

attributions.surface_quote: The seven worlds represent the rising grades of heavenly pleasure.

canonical_statement: The efficacy of ritual action is contingent upon precise alignment with temporal and cosmic conditions.

attributions.surface_quote: Certain times and conditions were regarded as peculiarly auspicious for performing sacrifice.

canonical_statement: The fire of wisdom is an internal process of refining thoughts, words, and deeds.

attributions.surface_quote: The real fire which every worshipper must light is the fire of wisdom.

canonical_statement: Ritualistic actions and good works performed for personal gain are ephemeral and do not lead to ultimate liberation.

attributions.surface_quote: all these sacrifices are inferior and ephemeral.

canonical_statement: Attachment to the fruits of action causes the soul to cycle repeatedly through birth, death, and suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: again and again come under the dominion of old age and death.

canonical_statement: Spiritual ignorance is characterized by the false belief that worldly success or ritual merit constitutes the highest good.

attributions.surface_quote: regard them as the highest good and delight in them.

canonical_statement: True spiritual guidance requires direct experiential vision rather than mere intellectual or scriptural learning.

attributions.surface_quote: no one save the man of direct vision shall venture to lead others.

canonical_statement: Egoism and vanity act as self-imposed bonds that prevent the individual from perceiving higher spiritual realities.

attributions.surface_quote: they bind themselves with their own vanity and egoism.

canonical_statement: Actions performed within the finite realm cannot produce permanent results.

attributions.surface_quote: man earns by finite actions, however good, cannot be permanent

canonical_statement: All individual beings originate from and ultimately return to an eternal, imperishable source.

attributions.surface_quote: all beings spring forth from the Imperishable and return thither again.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is infinite, formless, and transcends all biological and mental functions.

attributions.surface_quote: He is without form, without breath and without mind.

canonical_statement: The manifest universe, including physical elements and life-forces, is a direct emanation from the Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: From Him are born the life-force, mind, all sense organs, ether, air, fire, water and earth.

canonical_statement: The Absolute exists as the inner Self within all living beings.

attributions.surface_quote: He is the inner Self of all living beings.

canonical_statement: The distinction between the unconditioned Absolute and the creative, personal aspect of the Divine is fundamental to reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Nirguna-Brahman means Brahman without attributes, while Saguna-Brahman is God with attributes.

canonical_statement: The entirety of the manifest universe, including physical elements and living beings, originates from and is identical to the Supreme Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: All this is Brahman, the Highest Being.

canonical_statement: The individual self is composed of subtle layers including mind, intellect, and ego.

attributions.surface_quote: The inner self signifies the body made up of mind, intellect and ego.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality resides within the heart of the individual, and realizing this leads to liberation from ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: He who knows this Being dwelling in the cave of the heart cuts asunder ignorance.

canonical_statement: The physical world and its biological processes are manifestations of a divine causal hierarchy.

attributions.surface_quote: From Him come all herbs and juices, by which the inner self subsists.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Being is the foundational substrate of all existence, encompassing both manifest and unmanifest states.

attributions.surface_quote: In Him all is fixed... He is both formful and formless.

canonical_statement: Individual existence is ontologically dependent on the Supreme Being; nothing exists independently.

attributions.surface_quote: Nothing can exist apart from Him.

canonical_statement: The ultimate goal of the individual soul is to achieve non-dual union with the Supreme Being.

attributions.surface_quote: As the arrow becomes one with the mark, so will he become one with the Supreme.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Being is immanent within the heart of every individual.

attributions.surface_quote: The Supreme Lord abides in every heart.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is beyond the capacity of human conceptual understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: Who is beyond the reach of human understanding.

canonical_statement: Focused attention is a necessary prerequisite for the direct perception of ultimate reality.

attributions.surface_quote: If our mind is divided or scattered we cannot meditate.

canonical_statement: The individual soul, upon achieving direct perception, attains ontological unity with the Supreme.

attributions.surface_quote: We become one with the Supreme.

canonical_statement: The Supreme is the foundational substrate upon which all manifested existence and sensory phenomena depend.

attributions.surface_quote: There can be no form of manifested life apart from Him.

canonical_statement: The Atman dwells within the physical body, specifically centered in the heart, acting as the sustainer of life.

attributions.surface_quote: The seat of this Divine Principle in us is in the heart.

canonical_statement: The unchanging Atman appears to undergo emotional and mental modifications due to its interaction with the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: It appears to take the modifications of the mind.

canonical_statement: Realization of the Supreme dissolves the causal bonds of karma and eliminates the psychological fetters of ego and doubt.

attributions.surface_quote: The fetters of the heart are broken, all doubts are cut asunder.

canonical_statement: Intellectual analysis is insufficient for the realization of ultimate truth.

attributions.surface_quote: This does not happen when we gain intellectual knowledge only.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is a self-effulgent light that illuminates the entire universe.

attributions.surface_quote: When He shines, everything shines after Him.

canonical_statement: Direct realization of the divine dissolves the causal chains of karma.

attributions.surface_quote: all the chains of Karma past, present and future are shattered.

canonical_statement: The Supreme Brahman is omnipresent and constitutes the entirety of the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: The Supreme Brahman alone is the whole Universe.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and the Supreme Self coexist within the same body, one experiencing life and the other witnessing.

attributions.surface_quote: Two inseparable companions of golden plumage perch on the same tree.

canonical_statement: The individual soul is a reflection of the Supreme Soul, and the sense of ego creates the illusion of separation.

attributions.surface_quote: The Jiva or individual soul is merely the reflex of the Supreme Soul.

canonical_statement: Individual liberation requires the transcendence of both moral sin and merit, as both function as binding attachments to the ego.

attributions.surface_quote: sin is an iron chain, so merit can be a golden chain

canonical_statement: The ultimate state of being is characterized by the unification of the individual mind and will with the cosmic mind and will.

attributions.surface_quote: mind and will are completely unified with the cosmic mind and will

canonical_statement: The Supreme Reality is immanent within the human body yet transcends sensory perception and intellectual speculation.

attributions.surface_quote: subtler than the subtlest... yet here (in the body)

canonical_statement: Direct perception of the Absolute is only possible when the mind is purified and the senses are stilled through meditation.

attributions.surface_quote: when the mind is purified by the serene light of knowledge, then alone does the Seer perceive

attributions.surface_quote: energy manifests in five different forms through which the vital the body are Prana, Apana, Samana, Vyana and Udana

canonical_statement: Vital energy functions as the intermediary mechanism connecting external sensory data to the internal consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: senses are avenues through which the vital energy connects the outer world with the inner

canonical_statement: The soul's true nature is obscured by the accumulation of sensory impressions within the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: not until the mind is freed from these obscuring impressions can the soul manifest

canonical_statement: A purified mind achieves alignment with the cosmic will, causing individual desires to manifest through natural law.

attributions.surface_quote: his desires fulfill themselves by the natural course of law

canonical_statement: Realization of the Self involves recognizing the essential oneness between individual life and the cosmic totality.

attributions.surface_quote: a man's mind is purified, he realizes his oneness with the cosmic life

canonical_statement: The universe is grounded in and sustained by Brahman, which is the ultimate substrate of reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman, in which all this universe rests

canonical_statement: Desire acts as the causal seed for the cycle of birth, death, and mortal suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: Every desire is a seed from which spring birth, death and all mortal afflictions.

canonical_statement: The realization of the Self results in the immediate cessation of all desires.

attributions.surface_quote: he whose desires are fulfilled and who has known the Self, his desires vanish

canonical_statement: The Self is not attained through intellectual study but through a process of divine selection and revelation.

attributions.surface_quote: He whom the Self chooses, by him alone is It attained.

canonical_statement: Spiritual attainment requires the cultivation of inner vigor and the total renunciation of lower desires.

attributions.surface_quote: Self cannot be attained by one who is devoid of strength... or whose austerity is without renunciation.

canonical_statement: The individual self is ontologically identical to the all-pervading Spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: realizing the all-pervading Spirit present in all things, enter into all.

canonical_statement: At liberation, the constituent parts of the individual being dissolve into the universal Source.

attributions.surface_quote: fifteen parts return to their source

canonical_statement: Liberation involves the transcendence of name and form while retaining the true entity of the self.

attributions.surface_quote: he does not lose his true entity

canonical_statement: The realization of Brahman results in the cessation of individual suffering and the attainment of immortality.

attributions.surface_quote: he overcomes grief he overcomes sin... he becomes immortal.

canonical_statement: The knower of Brahman becomes identical in nature to Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: He who knows that highest Brahman becomes like unto Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: It should not be studied by one who has not fulfilled the vow.

canonical_statement: The transmission of higher knowledge to the unprepared results in cognitive dissonance and spiritual regression.

attributions.surface_quote: To others it will bring only confusion of mind and impede their progress.
